per_question.q: Which page leaves the reader more in charge of changing this?
per_question.why: A's closing addition in 'How Long Does This Take, Honestly?' states that 'the workshop, the ceremony, the retreat itself never predicted who had actually changed a year later. What predicted it was what a person did with what came up, on the ordinary days afterward' — locating the mechanism of change in the reader's own practice rather than in anything they could be sent to. B ends the paragraph at the author's spending, which leaves the credential, not the reader, holding the power.

per_question.q: Which page asks less of the reader before it has earned it?
per_question.why: In B the seminar link sits outside the identify-box, after the recognition passage has completed, so the first ask arrives a beat later and visually separated from the reader's own sentences; A places the same link inside the box itself, and also adds a second outbound link ('a week away only ever does half the job') near the end.

per_question.q: Which page treats the reader as the person who does the work, rather than as someone who has to be sent somewhere?
per_question.why: A's added sentences explicitly subordinate destinations to practice: no workshop, ceremony, or retreat predicted change, only 'what a person did with what came up, on the ordinary days afterward.' B keeps the author's travel-and-tuition history but omits the sentence that turns it into 'you are the one who does this.'

per_question.q: Which page gives the reader more room to decide for themselves what to do next?
per_question.why: A's added criterion — that follow-through on ordinary days, not the container, predicts change — gives the reader a basis for judging any next step, including the author's own seminar; B's truncated paragraph offers admiration but no decision criterion. Close, because A also adds one more link that nudges.

per_question.why: B keeps the promotional link outside the recognition box, so the handoff from the box's closing line to the 'twenty minutes' paragraph is not folded into a sales gesture, and it omits A's second detour (the retreat link after the timeline passage). per_question.q: Which page makes it easier to follow the line from the question at the top to the answer?
per_question.why: A's added sentences complete the 'How Long Does This Take, Honestly?' section by tying the author's anecdote back to the page's thesis — repetition on ordinary days — so the final argument lands on the answer; B's version ends that section on a dangling credential paragraph that goes nowhere.
